title: Reuse a valid host-known output size instead of reading a CUDA scalar
applies_when: A Torch metadata helper sizes an allocation such as arange from a device cumulative-length scalar, while the real caller already has the exact valid token count in host-side tensor shape or scheduler metadata.
lesson: Trace the caller before changing the helper: pass the existing exact host count through the API rather than converting a CUDA scalar or recomputing the count on the device. Test mappings, empty/interior-zero sequences, output dtype/device and the old optional-input behavior. Run the unchanged CUDA path under synchronization detection as a positive control, then the revised path under the same control. Loading a genuinely standalone helper directly can verify its real Torch operations without inventing backend mocks, but report this as component evidence and review the production wiring separately.
avoid_when: A padded tensor's capacity, graph bucket size or stale scheduler value may not equal the valid count. Do not silently replace data-dependent lengths with those values. Sync-debug mode is incomplete: passing it does not prove that every operation is asynchronous. A removed scalar read is not a whole-model speedup or proof of production graph-capture compatibility; use matched workload evidence for those claims.

evidence.note: Open, unmerged V4 prefill fix passes input_ids.numel() to the real caller. Reported native Torch 2.11/RTX 4060 helper evidence detects the original CUDA scalar synchronization and passes 26 CPU/CUDA component tests after the change. Full package/serving performance and upstream CI are not established.
Official documentation describes warn/error synchronization detection and warns that some synchronizing operations are not covered. It is a scoped diagnostic, not a completeness certificate.
